claims.text: Rapid solidification of a Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy creates a metastable microstructure containing nanoscale Mg-rich regions.
Modest thermal exposure transforms metastable Mg-rich regions into stable Mg-bearing intermetallic compounds.
The resulting microstructural evolution promotes formation of protective Mg-Al oxide layers during high-temperature oxidation.
Transformation of the Mg-rich regions alters local galvanic couples.
The altered microstructure reduces corrosion rates relative to the as-cast state.
The as-solidified alloy contains a solid solution, metastable nanoscale Mg-rich domains, and minor intermetallic particles.
A moderate post-solidification anneal can trigger transformation of the metastable domains into more stable intermetallic compounds.
Transformation and redistribution of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds mediate formation of localized protective Mg-Al oxide scales.
Thermal activation causes diffusion-driven separation of Mg from a supersaturated metastable matrix.
Diffusion-driven Mg separation produces stable Mg-containing intermetallic phases.
Mg-containing intermetallic phases act as preferential nucleation and growth sites for adherent protective oxides.
The altered interfacial chemistry reduces the number of active corrosion sites.
A continuous protective film limits the high-temperature oxidation rate.
Annealed samples will have a lower corrosion rate than the as-cast baseline under identical corrosive exposure.
Annealed samples will exhibit lower high-temperature oxidation weight gain than the as-cast baseline.
The as-solidified baseline lacks a continuous protective oxide layer.
The proposed mechanism applies only when thermal treatment does not cause full homogenization or a fully equilibrated microstructure.
The comparison uses the same alloy in as-cast and controlled-annealed conditions under identical corrosion and oxidation environments.
Failure to observe statistically significant corrosion and oxidation improvements after annealing is designated as a falsifying outcome.
Failure to observe stable Mg-bearing intermetallic formation or protective oxide formation is designated as a falsifying outcome.
